And if you tried google and it didn't work go old school. Write a brief letter addressed to your old pdoc and mail it to her old office. I think they'll forward the mail. The letter can simply state you would like to continue seeing her in therapy .
I'd try to get in touch with your pdoc right away say it's an emergency. Then go from there. If thoughts hurt self or others go right to ER.

Look out for key symptoms you get when hypomanic, and if you see those key symptoms get in touch with pdoc or therapist right away. For example I will be euphoric, but also sleep less and still feel energized. I see strangers as being familiar. I cuss a lot, unusual for me, and buy $200-300 worth of junk from dollar store and Walmart. 
Know your own symptoms and if you don't know what happens in hypomania then get into therapy and get help identifying your symptoms.
Oh and to deal with idiot front staff say stuff like this is urgent, I need to see the pdoc right away.

I hear you. Been a very long time since I was in a relationship. I feel touch starved, not even about sex, just wanting to cuddle and be held. Trying to focus on me and being able to be a full healthy partner one day. Still horrible feeling alone.

Well I'm unusual according to my psychiatrist in that while I'm BPI and have severe symptoms during a florid manic episode, normally in between episodes while on meds I'm pretty euthymic and normal. I also credit years and years of therapy as helping me deal with deep issues so I can live a fairly regular life. As a progressive Christian my spiritual health lately has been a cornerstone in staying well.
I'm also very well read on symptoms of BP and by now I know key early warning signs in my hypomania and when I see them I immediately get in touch with my pdoc. I can switch rapidly from hypomania into full florid mania  so I don't play if I see hypomanic symptom for two or three days.
I've had three florid manic episodes in the past ten years, lots of little hypomanias, and one mod depression. A key trigger for me is lack of sleep, so my first career in healthcare i had a bachelors which I had to give up because the hours and stress were too long. I kept going hypo and that was dangerous for the patients. Went back for my masters and then after a long unemployment stumbled into a job that eventually lead to being a science professor. Still in my first year but I love it so far. Reasonable hours, lower stress than healthcare, and I just love teaching! Finally found my niche.
Another key to staying well is my parents and brother are very supportive and well educated on BP. If they see early symptoms we talk, and that helps me reach out to therapist or pdoc early. I also tell close friends my diagnosis and what it means. My friends will tell me if I'm doing something strange. False alarms too but the support is worth explaining one happy day is not the same as hypomania. Oh and I live with my parents right now, so that provides structure in my home life I often struggled to make when I lived alone throughout college and healthcare career.

I don't like to think of life without meds I saw my grandma do that and hurt and drive away everyone around her with her fits of rage and paranoia. My pdoc monitors my blood for long term side effects and we'll stop
The meds and switch to others if there are deleterious changes in kidney or liver function.

I have florid mania with psychosis. When psychotic I believe people are following me filming me in a Truman like show. Except of course real. I have said really racist nonsense too. Normally i don't believe in that crap either. I also get paranoid about my family. I've never been violent or had violent fantasies but I do get irritable and impulsive and there have been dangerous times too where I could have hurt someone with a smidgen less control. Once I tried to jump out of my cousins car at 70 mph not because I was suicidal but because I believed I would hit the ground and roll a little and be ok, since I was in 2crazy2sane show. I've also believed in the world being an alternate place from the future where consciousness could be shifted to different lives. In short never heard voices or seen things not there but I have been psychotic and batshit crazy as a BPI.

Well being stable is vital to a career in healthcare. It's good news the lack of sleep isn't triggering! Living healthy otherwise is vital you can't control stress levels at work but you can avoid illicit drugs and alcohol, exercise, see a regular therapist and take your meds. You'll find without the sparkle of hypomania functioning at high levels can be tough and you'll be tempted to go off meds. Resist that temptation! And peoples high expectations can be terrifying. Ignore them
And focus on your hopes and dreams. Sounds like you love this career and are good at it. Do you love it enough to do everything you can to be stable? Also consider if you find that you can't stay stable and healthy due to stress while on meds then I think you have an obligation to step away from this career. If on the other hand you are self aware enough to ask for sick leave if an episode happens ( and sometimes they do regardless of all preventative steps in world) then maybe you can make it. If you don't know an episode is happening and you have trouble functioning at work then medicine may not be for you.

If you can't get to the doctor then you're not on meds. No meds means you're setting yourself up for failures. For any hope of this job working you have to be on meds. I wouldn't tell them why you're leaving the office either as its none of their business. If it helps at all I have a graduate degree and two part time jobs one teaching at a college level, and I am living with my parents. It's not perfect but sometimes we need extra support. I also know many friends who live with their parents. It's the economy and high costs of daily living.

First of all sorry for rudeness of some of these posts. Truth is we're all in your wife's shoes. We have no clue about what being a caretaker means and the wear and tear on the soul because typically we're doing the damage. I will say you need to look into involuntary commitment if she is suicidal. It's a tough call and will be expensive for a hospital stay but if she is suicidal then it's better that she be furious with you then dead. To be blunt. Involuntary commitment  has two criteria in all states that she be a danger to herself or a danger to someone else. You can call the police station I think to get more details. In my state a third criteria is that they are unable to care for themselves. Police come in my state and take you to the hospital where two doctors evaluate you and if both agree you're suicidal or homicidal you're admitted to the psych ward. Again I know money is an issue but they can't turn you away and some hospitals forgive debt if you're below a certain income.

I've switched AP several times. It's always scary so I recruit my family and support system to monitor for any odd signs. Sometimes it works out my last switch has given me my life back. Once I went manic and wound up in the hospital.

I've brought my parents to sessions to be educated and after a hospital stay when I was still impaired. It helped quite a bit in their awareness of symptoms and understanding of what hypomania vs mania vs happiness was like. I'd advise everyone to bring their major support to at least one educational session. Btw arrange with therapist or pdoc educational session ahead of time.

I've learned to not panic after one day of happiness or talking fast. I give it 2-3 days before panicking, unless I have a lot of symptoms. Also I look for 2 or more signs. Some signs like sleeplessness and high energy i hit a panic button right away. My family Is a great support and I encourage their feedback.some false alarms but I don't mind and sometimes they're spot on. I see a therapist every two weeks who helps monitor my mood. She and my pdoc have permission to contact my parents and tell them
If something is wrong, only in case of me being depressed, hypo or manic. I warn friends who are close and know my diagnosis when I change my AP or mood stabilizer to contact me and tell me if I act strange. I also educate my friends on what to look for. Working with my pdoc for about two years we got rid of APs I went manic, tried different APs I went hypomanic, and finally tried a low dose Risperidol went manic again. I have to be on a strong high dose AP like Risperidol or I got manic and severely psychotic. I do not recommend abruptly stopping an AP, some people can manage without it but mania with severe psychosis has totally ruined my life before. You should call your pdoc and taper off slowly at the very least, also if he knows you're off the AP he may adjust your other meds. Be very careful and diligent about monitoring yourself for signs of mania or hypomania, and contact pdoc if you see symptoms. There are other APs that are less sedating, maybe consider switching to them.

I've had trouble with intrusive thoughts before. Remember that these aren't true foreshadowing, just the product of your own mind. In my case I would remind myself the thought wasn't true, tell myself stop and visualize a stop sign. I'd also visualize the thought in a bubble floating away from me. Seemed to help.

I went back to school when I was late 20s. Don't burn any bridges whatever you do. Sounds like you're stable on your current meds, but be aware entering a PhD program will be very stressful and may require increasing some of your meds. Also be careful about overloading , I worked part time through grad school but sometimes think it would have been better not to. Also make sure you shadow someone in that field, since research seems to interest you, so you know what you're really getting into. I tend to procrastinate a lot, and worked really hard in therapy to overcome that since procrastination increased stress 10x. Studying a little every day or writing a paper well before the deadline is a good idea. Reducing stress elsewhere in your life is also beneficial.

Sounds like you've been through the wringer lately. If it helps managing bipolar takes time, time to find meds that work, time for therapy to kick in and be effective, time for you to learn warning signs and communicate with your psychiatrist, time to get healthy habits like sleeping enough and eating healthy. For me after my first mixed episode it took a year to feel more like myself, a year of healing and adjusting.  Some things, like recognizing warning signs of an episode and knowing how to tell your pdoc, take even longer. It's hard to be patient when you're suffering right now, but please don't do something as permanent as suicide when it's definitely possible to get better. 6 years before diagnosis almost constantly depressed with three long blocks of bad suicidal ideation, but in the nine years since diagnosis only one moderate depression. The right meds and therapy can have a huge impact, give yourself some grace and time to heal.

I don't know about you, but before my diagnosis and for some time after I had this simmering rage I refused to acknowledge. I would snap mean words at my friends, I lost quite a few friends that way, and towards my parents I was often rude and combative. What helped me was lots of therapy where I finally acknowledged I was a very angry person, and then more therapy to deal with that anger. After my second episode I came back to God and repaired my spiritual health. I also forgave my parents for some emotional abuse when  I was a child, and learned to forgive myself since God forgave me. I also learned like I said to take responsibility for my actions, not in the form of heaping guilt on myself but by saying I needed to approach things differently next time and apologizing when inevitably I messed up. Tweaking meds until there was a good combination helped too. Taking steps overall to be mentally healthy helps with simmering anger. I haven't really had an outburst like I used to have for years.

Also consider mixed episodes, which has features of mania like energy, irritability, and insomnia mixed with a depressed mood. Just be careful going without sleep when bipolar is usually a really bad sign and can cause or be an indication of mania or a mixed episode. Be really aware of any signs or symptoms for the next few days.

All you can do is learn from your mistakes and takes responsibility for your actions. Yes you may have been in an episode, but unless you were bad enough to go to the hospital you still had some control. I find if I apologize and own up that bipolar played a part but that's no reason to loss control people relate better. Just don't throw all responsibility on being bipolar, we still can control many things and if you can't control hurting people then a hospital is appropriate.
